fixes.explanation: Close, but that's not what the text says. The divisions were on rotating military duty each month throughout the year (1 Chronicles 27:1). So each division had its own month, and each one had 24,000 men. Even I take a break from stamping, and I'm made of metal.

Good guess, but the list doesn't say that. It says the divisions were on rotating military duty each month throughout the year (1 Chronicles 27:1). Wartime never comes up here at all. It's a month-by-month rotation, like a chore chart that actually got followed. I've never seen one of those in my whole kitchen.

Nope, that's not the group the text names. It says David did not count the men aged twenty or under (1 Chronicles 27:23). That's the group he left out of the count. Sixty never comes up in this passage at all.

Not this time, baker. The text says "…the number was not entered in the Book of the Chronicles of King David." (1 Chronicles 27:24). So the answer was True. That count never made it into that book, and I'd call that a very short entry.
